You are a programming expert.

        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 7d6b60dbc6a015dbdc444e4d39549600f7156690 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Date: Tue, 16 Jul 2019 13:49:30 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] drm/i915/execlists: Cancel breadcrumb on preempting the
 virtual engine

As we unwind the requests for a preemption event, we return a virtual
request back to its original virtual engine (so that it is available for
execution on any of its siblings). In the process, this means that its
breadcrumb should no longer be associated with the original physical
engine, and so we are forced to decouple it. Previously, as the request
could not complete without our awareness, we would move it to the next
real engine without any danger. However, preempt-to-busy allowed for
requests to continue on the HW and complete in the background as we
unwound, which meant that we could end up retiring the request before
fixing up the breadcrumb link.

Fixes: 22b7a426bbe1 ("drm/i915/execlists: Preempt-to-busy")
Signed-off-by: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Cc: Tvrtko Ursulin <tvrtko.ursulin@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Tvrtko Ursulin <tvrtko.ursulin@intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20190716124931.5870-4-chris@chris-wilson.co.uk
---
 drivers/gpu/drm/i915/gt/intel_lrc.c | 13 +++++++++++++
 1 file changed, 13 insertions(+)

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/gt/intel_lrc.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/gt/intel_lrc.c
index d076d9148b6d..dce36482a252 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/gt/intel_lrc.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/gt/intel_lrc.c
@@ -495,6 +495,19 @@ __unwind_incomplete_requests(struct intel_engine_cs *engine)
 			list_move(&rq->sched.link, pl);
 			active = rq;
 		} else {
+			/*
+			 * Decouple the virtual breadcrumb before moving it
+			 * back to the virtual engine -- we don't want the
+			 * request to complete in the background and try
+			 * and cancel the breadcrumb on the virtual engine
+			 * (instead of the old engine where it is linked)!
+			 */
+			if (test_bit(DMA_FENCE_FLAG_ENABLE_SIGNAL_BIT,
+				     &rq->fence.flags)) {
+				spin_lock(&rq->lock);
+				i915_request_cancel_breadcrumb(rq);
+				spin_unlock(&rq->lock);
+			}
 			rq->engine = owner;
 			owner->submit_request(rq);
 			active = NULL;
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by the failure to decouple the breadcrumb of a virtual request from its original physical engine when preempting the virtual engine. This oversight allowed the request to potentially complete in the background while still being linked to the original engine, leading to a situation where the request could be retired before the breadcrumb link was properly updated. This resulted in list corruption, as indicated by the error message about `list_del corruption` and the presence of `LIST_POISON1`, which signifies that the list structure was in an invalid state due to improper handling of the request's lifecycle during preemption.

This oversight allowed the request to potentially complete in the background while still being linked to the original engine, leading to a situation where the request could be retired before the breadcrumb link was properly updated. This resulted in list corruption, as indicated by the error message about `list_del corruption` and the presence of `LIST_POISON1`, which signifies that the list structure was in an invalid state due to improper handling of the request's lifecycle during preemption.
